turns.question: can I retire early without losing too much?
turns.answer:
You can retire now under Article 11 because you are age 55 or older, have at least 10 years of service, and have 20 or more years of service. The applicable early-retirement provision allows an age-and-service annuity based on your accumulated credits, computed at your age when you leave. [40 ILCS 5/11-130]

Section 11-134 also reaches an employee with at least 20 years of service who retires before age 60. For the formula used here, the annuity is reduced by 0.25% for each month the annuity begins before age 60. The Code also provides an alternative annuity election under that section. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

On the figures available, the estimate is:

- **$32,126.78 per year**
- **$2,677.23 per month**

**What I assumed:** you stop working today, September 13, 2026.

The special early-retirement incentives in Sections 11-133.1 and 11-133.2 do not establish a current retirement benefit on the facts available because they require specific past application and withdrawal windows. [40 ILCS 5/11-133.1] [40 ILCS 5/11-133.2]

I could not establish whether any alternative calculation or service credit under provisions such as Sections 11-150, 11-221, or former Section 20-122 would affect your benefit because those provisions were not available here.

turns.question: what is Article 11?
turns.answer:
Article 11 creates and governs the **Laborers’ and Retirement Board Employees’ Annuity and Benefit Fund** in each city with more than 500,000 inhabitants. [40 ILCS 5/11-101]

It defines the Article’s key terms, including “fund” and “annuity.” An annuity generally means equal monthly payments for life, subject to the termination rules named in Section 11-124. [40 ILCS 5/11-102] [40 ILCS 5/11-103] [40 ILCS 5/11-124]

The Article also addresses eligibility, retirement annuities, survivor and disability benefits, contributions, refunds, and administration. Section 11-125 excludes certain categories of people, including some temporary employees, people eligible for another applicable retirement fund, and certain individuals entering service at older ages. [40 ILCS 5/11-125]

I’m going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that’s not right.
